name: OBSC Perfection Ltd
tagline: Precision-machining SME with a Rs 1,200 Cr order book on ~Rs 190 Cr revenue and a defence/marine mix shift — execution and margin-sustainability unproven
business_overview: OBSC Perfection (IPO 2024, NSE SME) makes precision metal components — historically machined/cast auto parts, now adding a first-ever in-house forging plant (hot + cold) in Pune and diversifying into defence, marine, renewable-energy and (nascent) aerospace parts. Operates from 4-5 fragmented factories in a Gujarat/Chennai tier-2 base, with land acquired to consolidate into an integrated facility.
fundamentals_narrative: Growth and return ratios look strong for an SME, but the market prices ~12x sales, discounting years of flawless execution. The Rs 1,200 Cr order book is ~6x revenue and skews toward higher-margin defence/marine, supporting management's aim to lift the defence/marine mix toward 50% over 3-5 years (auto-component margins are stated at 10-15%, marine/defence pull the blended OPM to ~18%). Rising land/plant additions (Sanand machining unit, ~Rs 49 Cr/yr incremental from Q4 FY27; Maharashtra integrated facility) are the near-term capex.
technical_read: Not pulled — SME liquidity; stock has re-rated hard since IPO.
sentiment_summary: First-time deep read — last ~22 of ~34 posts, Oct 2025 to May 2026. Active, high-quality thread: multiple members did plant visits (Chennai, Pune) and peer analysis vs Sansera/RACL. Bull view: huge book-to-bill, credible defence/marine scale-up, well-connected parent (decades of ties to large auto-component groups), 'fire in the belly' management. Persistent skeptic thread: employee cost as % of sales is implausibly low versus Sansera/RACL — explained (not fully resolved) as heavy job-work/contract-labour outsourcing (809 contract workers Mar-25), which shifts cost to job-work charges and could mean OBSC does mostly finishing/assembly, not the hard machining it claims. Only one concall a year.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users. Non-roster contributors raj1968, Chandragupta, manpritaurora, richbandit, Satishwe carried a substantive, mixed debate (loves 6-26). The X trigger (@LearningEleven, non-roster, stated holder — 'going from scale to scale') is a vetted tip, treated as informational only.
bull_case: ~Rs 1,200 Cr order book on ~Rs 190 Cr revenue, largely nominated (low cancellation risk), with a defence/marine mix shift that is margin-accretive
First in-house forging capacity augments existing machining/casting — a real capability step, with orders already in hand
~18% ROCE, ~25% growth, low debt, integrated-facility consolidation ahead
Parent's long-standing relationships with large auto-component groups underpin order flow
bear_case: Employee cost is anomalously low vs precision-engineering peers — unresolved question over how much true machining is in-house vs outsourced job-work
~12x sales prices near-flawless multi-year execution; post-IPO SMEs frequently see margins fade
Once-a-year concall = thin disclosure; scaling complex machining/forging from a small, fragmented base is hard
Rising debtor days flagged; capex-funding and working-capital needs grow with the order book

value_chain.theme: Precision machined/forged components for auto, defence, marine, renewables
value_chain.position: Tier-2/Tier-1 component supplier; nominated auto business is sticky, defence/marine is the value-add push
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Skilled shop-floor machining capacity and defence/marine qualification (long approval cycles)
value_chain.note: Order book implies the demand-side is secured; the open question is whether OBSC's own capacity/skill (vs outsourced job-work) can execute the machining content at the stated margins.

verdict_headline: Credible high-growth SME story — order book supports it, but valuation and the outsourcing/margin question keep conviction at Medium
verdict_reasoning: Small-cap with strong recent growth and a specific, credible catalyst (a 6x book-to-bill order book weighted to margin-accretive defence/marine) — fits '10x-in-2-3-years' at LOW-MEDIUM conviction with an 'unconfirmed' caveat on margin sustainability.
X signal (@LearningEleven, non-roster, x_conviction 'high') informational only — no conviction floor.

Two unresolved risks — the implausibly low employee cost (outsourced job-work vs genuine in-house machining) and ~12x-sales valuation — cap conviction at Medium pending the next annual concall / FY27 execution.

four_box.note: Defence/marine mix-shift (target 50% of revenue in 3-5yrs) is a real margin-accretive tailwind; Rs1,200cr order book (~6x revenue) supports tam; nominated-auto stickiness + defence/marine qualification cycles are a real barrier but unresolved whether in-house machining vs outsourced job-work (employee-cost anomaly) — moat weak; ~12x sales already prices near-flawless execution — valuation no.
